pr_body:
Fixes #47145

Instead of doing some butchery with atan and then manipulating angles, we simply rotate the vector.

There is still a singularity if the direction vector is parallel to the local Y axis. This is however only noticeable if the flatness is set to != 0.
This can't be avoided, unless we allow the user to specify a custom up-vector.
pr_comments: I'm not sure that Y axis is a good idea to pick as a point of singularity. I see it as being used way more often than other directions (for example a random (0.5,0.2,0.3) (not normalized, I know)) seems like a safer bet to me.

Also, this PR needs to target 4.0 and then be cherry picked for 3.x. 

Let me know if you need help rebasing this on the 4.0 branch.
@clayjohn I think that having a singularity that happens in one of the most common use cases is not a good approach

issue_context.title: ParticlesMaterial's emission direction is wrong if direction.z != 0 and direction.y != 0
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
v3.2.4-rc5


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10. GLES3.


**Issue description:**
If the direction property of a ParticlesMaterial is changed, it often behaves completely unpredictable.
This is especially apparent, if the values are close to zero.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
The example has two particle systems, which are identical, save for the emission direction.
One of them has the vector (1.0, 0.0, 0.0), the other (1.0, 0.01, 0.01).
They should visually emit in almost the same direction, they are almost 45° off.

[particle_spread_test.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6167382/particle_spread_test.zip)
comments: Is this reproducible in the `master` branch too?

Yes, master has the same issue.

I had assumed there had been a rewrite for ParticlesMaterial.
Since master breaks compatibility, I would recommend redesigning ParticlesMaterial anyway.
The way it currently is, isn't really that pretty.

For spread I would do the following:
- Remove the direction, just emit along a constant axis. If needed, the Node can be rotated already.
- Add a separate external_velocity vector that is added on top of the computed velocity.

> Remove the direction, just emit along a constant axis. If needed, the Node can be rotated already.

The Direction property was originally added here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/26613

I wouldn't remove it again given how many people seem to rely on it even now.

Hm, yeah, I forgot about emitting with local coordinates...
Then I suppose at least a user controlled Up vector should be introduced.

Possible duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/30340

Can you check and see if #47146 fixes #30340?

It should fix that too, yes.
But that issue mentions the documentation, and that says:
>float spread
>Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees. Applied to X/Z plane and Y/Z planes.

The new implementation doesn't match that, but neither did the old one, I suppose...
The spread is now applied in the plane that is orthogonal to the _direction_.
